points.en: Demand-Pull Inflation: Excess aggregate demand over supply (Too much money chasing too few goods).
points.hi: Demand-Pull Inflation: Excess aggregate demand over supply (Too much money chasing too few goods).

points.en: Cost-Push Inflation: Rising production costs (wages, raw materials) forcing firms to hike prices.
points.hi: Cost-Push Inflation: Rising production costs (wages, raw materials) forcing firms to hike prices.

points.en: Monetary Expansion: Excessive money supply growth by the central bank leading to currency devaluation.
points.hi: Monetary Expansion: Excessive money supply growth by the central bank leading to currency devaluation.

points.en: Structural Bottlenecks: Supply chain disruptions, poor infrastructure, or hoarding causing supply shortages.
points.hi: Structural Bottlenecks: Supply chain disruptions, poor infrastructure, or hoarding causing supply shortages.

explanation.en: D: Demand-Pull, C: Cost-Push, M: Monetary Expansion, S: Structural Bottlenecks.
explanation.hi: D: Demand-Pull, C: Cost-Push, M: Monetary Expansion, S: Structural Bottlenecks.

answer.en: Inflation caused by an increase in aggregate demand that outpaces the economy's production capacity.
answer.hi: Inflation caused by an increase in aggregate demand that outpaces the economy's production capacity.

misconception.en: Inflation is always caused by government spending.
misconception.hi: Inflation is always caused by government spending.

correction.en: Inflation can also be caused by supply-side shocks, global commodity price hikes, or private sector credit expansion.
correction.hi: Inflation can also be caused by supply-side shocks, global commodity price hikes, or private sector credit expansion.

fiveFacts.en: Demand-pull is often associated with economic booms.
fiveFacts.hi: Demand-pull is often associated with economic booms.

fiveFacts.en: Cost-push is often associated with supply shocks (e.g., oil price spikes).
fiveFacts.hi: Cost-push is often associated with supply shocks (e.g., oil price spikes).

fiveFacts.en: Inflation reduces the purchasing power of money.
fiveFacts.hi: Inflation reduces the purchasing power of money.

fiveFacts.en: RBI uses monetary policy (Repo rate) to control demand-pull inflation.
fiveFacts.hi: RBI uses monetary policy (Repo rate) to control demand-pull inflation.

fiveFacts.en: Structural inflation is common in developing economies due to supply chain inefficiencies.
fiveFacts.hi: Structural inflation is common in developing economies due to supply chain inefficiencies.

threeTraps.en: Assuming all price rises are inflation (must be sustained and general).
threeTraps.hi: Assuming all price rises are inflation (must be sustained and general).

threeTraps.en: Confusing inflation with a one-time price adjustment.
threeTraps.hi: Confusing inflation with a one-time price adjustment.

threeTraps.en: Ignoring the role of expectations in driving wage-price spirals.
threeTraps.hi: Ignoring the role of expectations in driving wage-price spirals.
